question.problem: Given that ${3}^{4-2x}=\sqrt{2},$ find the value of $x$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Taking ${log}_{3}$ of both sides of the equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{4-2x} & =\sqrt{2} \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{4-2x}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(\sqrt{2}) \\ 4-2x & ={log}_{3}⁡({2}^{1/2})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side:

$$
4-2x=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{3}⁡(2)
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4-2x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\ -2x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}-4 \\ x & =2-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{4\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
x≈1.842
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places
